summary_en: The delightful blend of scares and chuckles in Apple TV+'s Widow's Bay has captured audiences worldwide. If you're already hooked on its unique charm, here are five other series that offer similar thrills and quirky characters to tide you over.

en.title: Widow's Bay Fans: 5 Shows to Binge While Waiting for Season 2
en.summary: The delightful blend of scares and chuckles in Apple TV+'s Widow's Bay has captured audiences worldwide. If you're already hooked on its unique charm, here are five other series that offer similar thrills and quirky characters to tide you over.
en.body:
The television landscape of 2026 has delivered a gem in **Widow's Bay**. This Apple TV+ original, lauded for its masterful balance of spooky small-town horror and laugh-out-loud comedy, has quickly become a fan favorite. Its instantly iconic characters, including **Tom**, **Wyck**, **Patricia**, **Rosemary**, and **Bechir**, have cemented its place as one of the year's standout series. As we eagerly await news of a potential second season, the question on everyone's mind is: what can we watch to fill the void?

While no show is *exactly* like **Widow's Bay**, several series capture its spirit of weirdness, supernatural intrigue, and compelling character work. We're steering clear of the obvious comparisons like **Twin Peaks** or **The X-Files** – you've likely already devoured those. Instead, we're diving into some gems that might have flown under your radar, offering that perfect mix of the unsettling and the hilarious.

## Embracing the Wild and Wacky

Television is currently enjoying a renaissance of delightfully bizarre storytelling, and **Widow's Bay** is at the forefront. If you're drawn to its surreal humor and conspiracy-tinged narrative, you might find a kindred spirit in **The Chair Company**. This HBO Max series, created by **Tim Robinson** and **Zach Kanin**, masterfully blends comedy and surrealism. Its premise – a man who suffers a humiliating fall during a promotion speech and becomes obsessed with a broken chair – is just the beginning of a hilariously offbeat conspiracy thriller. For fans of **Tim Robinson's** signature comedic style seen in **I Think You Should Leave**, **The Chair Company** offers a similar brand of offbeat characters and escalating absurdity. While some viewers have found it *too* strange, its unique vision is precisely what makes it a compelling watch for those who crave the truly unconventional.

## Animated Escapades and Heartwarming Dramas

Beyond the realm of live-action oddities, animated series can also deliver that perfect blend of mystery and heart. **Gravity Falls**, created by **Alex Hirsch**, is a prime example. This Disney Channel series, while aimed at a younger audience, is celebrated for its sharp writing, intricate mysteries, and surprisingly mature themes that resonate deeply with adults. Its small-town setting, secret conspiracies, and a cast of quirky characters make it an ideal follow-up for **Widow's Bay** fans looking for engaging storytelling and a touch of the supernatural. For those who prefer their compelling narratives with a dose of genuine warmth and character development, **Ted Lasso** remains a benchmark. Though a drama, its optimistic outlook and focus on building community, much like the found family in **Widow's Bay**, offers a different, yet equally satisfying, viewing experience. The show's universally acclaimed run has left a lasting impact, proving that heartfelt storytelling can be just as addictive as supernatural thrillers.

## What's Next

While a second season for **Widow's Bay** has not yet been officially announced, the success of its first outing strongly suggests more is to come. In the meantime, these highly-regarded series offer ample opportunity to dive into new worlds and discover your next binge-worthy obsession.

content_raw: There isn’t a show around that’s exactly like Widow’s Bay . Katie Dippold’s new Apple TV original has definitely struck a chord with audiences in 2026, maintaining a delicate balance between scares and chuckles and introducing us to instantly iconic characters like Tom, Wyck, Patricia , Rosemary, and Bechir. But there are shows out there that manage to do spooky small-town horror or silly supernatural shenanigans well enough to devote your time to as you wait for a second season of Widow’s Bay . We’re going to assume you’ve already seen (or passed on) some of the bigger shows that Widow’s Bay’ s humor and horror have been compared to, like Twin Peaks or The X-Files . Instead, we’re going to focus on some of the other series that may have slipped by you over the years. The Chair Company Isn’t it wonderful that television is once again embracing its wild, weird and wacky side? And right up there with Widow’s Bay in this endeavor we have The Chair Company , which combines comedy and surrealism in a way that no one else has quite managed. With one season available to binge on HBO Max and more in the offing, Tim Robinson and Zach Kanin’s bonkers story of a man who gets a promotion, falls on his ass during his big speech and then gets fixated on finding out why his chair broke is sublime, and you can now get in on the ground floor of what promises to be one of TV’s oddest conspiracy thrillers. If you’re already a fan of Robinson’s I Think You Should Leave style of comedy and enjoy shows with offbeat characters, The Chair Company might be for you. However, it’s worth noting that the show has been divisive for some, who’ve found it just too weird for its own good. Round the Twist This Australian curio from the early 1990s would never be made today! It’s essentially a show for kids , but you’ll definitely be asking yourself how anyone thought it was entirely appropriate for them. Landing somewhere between The Adventures of Pete & Pete , The Twilight Zone and a fever dream, Round the Twist focuses on the boisterous Twist family, who move to a lighthouse in the town of Port Niranda and end up encountering a whole bunch of supernatural weirdness. Boasting a theme song that will never leave your brain and four seasons full of episodes that constantly push the boundaries of kids’ TV, Round the Twist is weird, funny, creepy, and utterly gross. Essential cult viewing for those who miss boundless imagination on a tight budget. Midnight Mass After a former venture capitalist kills a woman in a drunk-driving accident and ends up serving four years in jail for the crime, he returns to his hometown of Crockett Island looking for a fresh start.
